products.summary: The Products feature is a small Odoo-style catalog (Product + ProductCategory) inside the Sales module. Frontend surface is one page (apps/web/src/pages/ProductsPage.tsx) at /sales/products wired through SalesRoutes.tsx, lazyPages.tsx, navConfig.ts and RouteAnnouncer.tsx, backed by React Query hooks in apps/web/src/hooks/useProducts.ts. API surface is apps/api/src/routes/products.ts (7 endpoints under /api/v1/products and /api/v1/products/categories, guarded by products:write RBAC) registered in server.routes.ts:53/132, with Zod schemas in packages/shared/src/schemas/products.ts (re-exported at schemas/index.ts:21). Prisma models Product (schema.prisma:2011-2036) and ProductCategory (1991-2009) are referenced by SalesOrderLine.productId (REQUIRED FK, ON DELETE RESTRICT, line 2081/2090), InvoiceLine.productId (optional FK, 2182/2191), QuoteLine.productId (dormant column with index but NO Prisma relation and no API exposure, 3069), and Subscription.productId (dormant column, 4142, unused at runtime). Sales order creation (NewSalesOrderPage.tsx + sales-orders.write.routes.ts:59-104) is built entirely around the catalog: every order line requires a productId, prices default from listPriceMicros, and currency mismatches are rejected. Invoices reference products optionally (invoiceLineProductIds + tenantEntitiesBelongToOrg('product', ...) in invoices.service.write.ts, invoices.ts, invoices.mutations.ts; read paths join product sku/name). Quotes do NOT reference the catalog at runtime — quote lines are freeform name/description. Opportunities have no productId; the "topProducts" in /api/reports/sales-intelligence comes from a name-classification heuristic (classifyProduct) plus readProductRollup raw SQL over the products table that degrades to [] if the table is absent. Seeds couple orders to products via productIdBySku (packages/db/src/seed.ts:335-396, sales-seed-data.products.ts, sales-seed-data.orders.ts:9,212-213), and RBAC seeds define products:read/products:write (seed.rbac.ts:60-61 plus role grant lists). A separate AccountProduct model (account-intel/document-extract feature) and the onboarding ProductTour share the word "product" but are unrelated and must NOT be touched. Command palette has zero product references; the only nav refs are sidebar + route announcer.

invoices.summary: Invoices is a complete quote-to-cash vertical: an Odoo account.move-style Invoice/InvoiceLine/Payment trio in Prisma, a Fastify plugin tree under /api/v1/invoices (list, detail, draft PATCH, create, create-from-order, send/cancel/pay transitions, partial payments, streaming CSV export, AR-aging report), Zod wire schemas in packages/shared/src/schemas/invoices.ts, and a React surface at /sales/invoices (list, new, detail with lines/payments/audit tables and a RecordPaymentCard). The route file apps/api/src/routes/invoices.ts registers three sub-plugins (mutations, payments, export) and the domain logic lives in apps/api/src/services/invoices/* ; a second copy at apps/api/src/services/crm/invoices.service.ts has zero importers (dead code). Payments are entirely a child feature of invoices — the Payment model requires invoiceId with cascade delete and there is no standalone payments route — so deleting invoices deletes all payment tracking. Coupling to sales orders is real: Invoice.salesOrderId FK, sales-orders.helpers.ts queries prisma.invoice to populate invoiceId on the order detail payload, the shared SalesOrderDetail schema exposes invoiceId, SalesOrderDetailPage renders Create Invoice / View Invoice CTAs, and POST /invoices/from-order/:orderId converts orders. Opportunities have no data coupling — only a code comment in opportunities.export.ts referencing the invoice CSV sanitizer. The Sales Dashboard consumes GET /api/invoices/ar-aging via useArAging + ArAgingCard, so deletion removes that widget's data source. Cross-cutting registries referencing invoices: RBAC permission keys (invoices:read/write in shared types, seed.rbac.ts, rbac-matrix test), webhook event keys invoice.sent/invoice.paid, custom-field entity type 'invoice', tenant-ownership entity map, audit-log target types and deep links, nav sidebar, lazy routes, RouteAnnouncer, command-palette/global-search type unions, notification pref invoiceOverdue, OrgSettings.invoicePrefix/invoiceNetDays columns, six locale pairs, and two e2e specs. Prisma migrations already shipped invoice tables (20260511050000_add_invoicing plus later drift/index migrations) — removal requires a new drop migration, never edits to existing ones. The BIDCRM-design/ directory holds a frozen parallel copy of the whole feature (snapshot, out of normal edit scope), and schema.prisma.backup/.pulled also contain the models.

A third adjacent feature, Agent Studio (/agent-studio, Crew/CrewAgent/CrewTask/CrewRun + crew.run worker), ships an 'RFP Response Crew' preset but is a separate codepath from the RFP Agent system. sales-dashboard.summary: There are two distinct global dashboard surfaces plus the account cockpit they compete with. (1) /sales renders SalesDashboardPage (apps/web/src/pages/SalesDashboardPage.tsx), an ERP-style sales dashboard with 14 widgets: a header source badge (ERP sale.order mirror vs Opportunity pipeline fallback) plus an Auto-populate enrichment button, 4 KpiTiles (Quotations/Orders/Revenue/Average Order with period deltas and drill-through to /sales/orders?state=), PipelineSnapshot, WinRateCard, MonthlySalesChart (custom 350-line SVG spline chart), Top Quotations, Top Sales Orders, TeamLeaderboard, TerritoryRevenueCard, TopCountriesCard, ArAgingCard, a Top Products inline table, Top Customers, and TopCategoriesTreemap. All of it is fed by ONE query — GET /api/reports/sales-intelligence (useSalesIntelligence hook) — except ArAgingCard (GET /api/invoices/ar-aging) and the autopopulate mutation (POST /api/crm/companies/autopopulate-from-sales). (2) /dashboard renders DashboardPage which branches: no accountId → OrgDashboard (apps/web/src/components/dashboard/OrgDashboard.tsx, 'Workspace Command Center') with ~15 widgets (SourceStat strip x6, KpiRow x6 org KPIs, InsightsBar, RecentActivityCard, TopAccountsCard, SalesFunnelCard, WorkspaceHealthCard with a client-side synthetic score, PipelineCard, PipelineByStageMini, 2 AlertCards, QuickActionsCard, WeeklyGoalCard with a hardcoded 500k EUR target, WinRateCard, QuickLinksCard), fed by /api/crm/summary, /api/crm/dashboard, and /api/reports/pipeline; with accountId → the account cockpit (the surface product feedback calls the core). Crucially, the dedicated backend /api/sales-dashboard/* surface (8 endpoints in apps/api/src/routes/sales-dashboard.ts + sales-dashboard.service.ts, aggregating Prisma SalesOrder/SalesOrderLine/Product/ProductCategory) is consumed by ZERO frontend code — only its own integration tests; the web went through /api/reports/sales-intelligence instead, which auto-falls back from sales_orders tables to the Opportunity pipeline via tableExists() guards. The account cockpit itself embeds SalesIntelligencePanel showing the same GLOBAL (org-wide) report, not account-scoped data. Minimal essentials on /sales are the 4 KPI tiles + MonthlySalesChart (and arguably PipelineSnapshot/WinRateCard); the global-pipeline bloat is the ERP leaderboard tail: TeamLeaderboard, TerritoryRevenueCard, TopCountriesCard, TopCategoriesTreemap, Top Products/Customers/Quotations/Orders lists, ArAgingCard, and the autopopulate enrichment control.

key-top-accounts.summary: Key Accounts and Top Accounts are two distinct org-scoped concepts sharing one API module. The Company prisma model carries tier (enum AccountTier: key | top | standard, default standard), keyAccountSince, keyAccountOwnerId, keyAccountNotes, and topAccountRank (Int?, never written by any code). Key accounts = companies manually flagged tier='key' via PATCH /api/v1/companies/:id/tier (guarded by accounts:write, validates owner belongs to org, auto-sets/clears keyAccountSince, writes an audit log entry); they are listed by GET /api/v1/accounts/key (cursor-paginated, search/industry/ownerId filters, aggregates pipeline/open deals/contacts). Top accounts = a purely auto-computed leaderboard: GET /api/v1/accounts/top ranks companies by SUM(opportunity value_micros) in raw SQL and assigns topAccountRank as the result index, ignoring the stored column. Frontend pages exist at /key-accounts (KeyAccountsPage, titled 'Strategic Accounts') and /top-accounts (TopAccountsPage, titled 'Account Ranking', limit 20), both in the sidebar 'Accounts' group. Critically, the tier PATCH endpoint has zero frontend callers — grep for 'tier' across apps/web/src matches only the two hooks and TopAccountsPage — so there is no UI anywhere to flag a key account, even though KeyAccountsPage's empty state tells users to do it 'from the Companies page'. No seed sets tier='key', so a demo DB renders the Key Accounts page empty. There is no manually-curated global top-10 concept at all: no model, endpoint, page, or Settings section supports pinning/ordering accounts; the tier value 'top' is a dead enum member nothing queries; the dashboard's TopAccountsCard despite its name just shows the first 5 companies from CRM dashboard data, not a ranked or curated list. Settings has 13 sections (profile, workspace, crm, rfp-analytics, etc.) with no account-curation surface.

bid-no-bid.summary: The Bid/No-Bid module is fully built end-to-end. Frontend: BidNoBidPage at /bid-matrix renders 10 weighted criteria cards (0-5 buttons), a ScoreSummaryStrip with overall ProgressRing + 4 per-category rings, an opportunity selector (?opportunityId= query param), Save Score / AI Calibrate / Defend Score buttons, and a free-text Decision Notes textarea. Backend: apps/api/src/routes/bid-scores.ts exposes list, latest-per-opportunity, create (versioned, RBAC bid-scores:write, MemOS L1 trace + L2 policy crystallization on extreme scores), ai-calibrate (heuristic — MemOS policy keyword matching + opportunity probability/value boosts; Dust is explicitly stubbed), and defend (real Dust execBrief agent call via defendBidScore in dust-agent.service.ts with heuristic fallback). Scores persist in Prisma model BidScore (table bid_scores, schema.prisma:2970-3008) with criteria Json, totalScore 0-100, categoryScores Json, weightedSum/totalWeight, aiSuggested, memosPolicies, recommendation (bid|no_bid|proceed_with_caution), notes, and a unique (orgId, opportunityId, version) — every save creates a new version. Opportunity detail surfaces the score via BidScoreCard (OpportunityDetailPage.tsx:262) showing only totalScore% + recommendation badge + a Details/Evaluate Now link to /bid-matrix — no per-criteria breakdown there. RfpResponseHubPage also lists recent scores and an avg-score KPI. Critically, frontend and backend criteria IDs diverge: frontend has margin_potential/payment_terms/timeline_risk while backend CRITERIA_WEIGHTS has profitability/timeline_fit/risk_profile, so payment_terms etc. are silently ignored in the persisted computation and AI Calibrate returns 3 IDs the UI cannot display. Recommendation thresholds also diverge (frontend conditional at >=55, backend at >=50). Nothing exists for below-threshold override, mandatory justification, or sharing to directors/VPs — no override fields, no Notification model, no Director/VP roles in seed.rbac.ts.

platform.summary: BidStack's platform layer is env-driven and pattern-consistent. apps/api validates ALL env at boot via a single Zod schema in apps/api/src/env.ts (envSchema + getEnv() with semantic cross-field checks: prod requires PUBLIC_BASE_URL non-localhost, STORAGE_DRIVER=s3 unless DEMO_MODE, INTEGRATION_TOKEN_KEY mandatory in prod, DEMO_MODE mutually exclusive with Clerk); apps/worker has NO Zod env module — it reads process.env directly with only a prod presence check for DATABASE_URL/REDIS_URL in apps/worker/src/main.ts:60-66; apps/web uses build-time VITE_* vars resolved in apps/web/vite.config.ts via loadEnv from the repo root, with auth mode baked at build (build/build:prod/build:demo scripts set VITE_AUTH_MODE=stub|clerk|demo). There is NO feature-flag system or library (no LaunchDarkly/Unleash/PostHog hits anywhere) — gating is env vars (DEMO_MODE, BIDSTACK_OCR_ENABLED, OPENAPI_DOCS_ENABLED, VITE_SSO_MICROSOFT_ENABLED, PREDICTIVE_USE_XGBOOST), per-org DB toggles (WebhookSubscription.active, IntegrationConfig.enabled), and RBAC preHandlers (server.requirePermission). Docker: one root multi-stage Dockerfile with targets base→builder→migrate|api|web|worker|mcp-server (non-root user, healthchecks, one-shot migrate stage), plus a standalone apps/worker/Dockerfile for Railway's RAILWAY_DOCKERFILE_PATH. Deploys: Vercel hosts the demo SPA (vercel.json buildCommand pnpm --filter @bidstack/web build:demo), Railway runs api+worker+Postgres+Redis per DEPLOY.md; infra/azure (main.bicep + draft workflow) is an explicitly UNVALIDATED Container Apps draft; docker-compose.yml/docker-compose.prod.yml are the validated local/prod topologies. CI: 7 workflows (.github/workflows/ci.yml with unit/secrets-full-scan/integration jobs, plus e2e, gitleaks, semgrep, dependency-review, lighthouse, tsdoc-coverage). apps/mcp-server is a Fastify host wrapping @modelcontextprotocol/sdk McpServer over Streamable HTTP (+legacy SSE), Bearer ApiKey auth → {orgId, scopes}, Redis-backed per-minute+hourly rate limits, and a tools registry (apps/mcp-server/src/tools/index.ts) where each tool is a {description, input Zod schema, inputJsonSchema, handler(args, ctx)} object with read/write scope mapping. External API client canon: packages/dust-client (class + fetch + Bearer + Zod-parsed responses + 429/5xx exponential backoff + timeout + pino) and packages/odoo-mcp-client (hand-rolled MCP streamable-HTTP JSON-RPC CLIENT, no SDK dep — the template for an InfoSearch MCP client). Webhooks: inbound /webhooks/dust (raw-body content parser, HMAC verify via verifyDustSignature, 5-min replay window, Redis SET NX dedup, persist SyncEvent, ack fast, worker does side effects) and outbound fan-out via fanOutWebhookEvent → BullMQ webhook.delivery queue → worker signs X-BidStack-Signature t=,v1= HMAC posts with retry/dead-letter/auto-disable.

notes: Conventions to replicate for a new vertical: (a) Prisma: uuid PK, orgId @map("org_id") + Org relation with onDelete Cascade, deletedAt soft delete, @@index([orgId]) + query-shaped composite indexes, @@map(snake_plural); (b) shared schemas: file packages/shared/src/schemas/<entity>.ts with X / XCreate / XPatch / XFilter / XPage / XSummary naming, z.infer type twins, barrel export with .js suffix; (c) API: routes/<entity>.ts exporting <entity>Routes: FastifyPluginAsyncZod, registered once in server.routes.ts with { prefix: '/api/v1' }; (d) web: hooks/use<Entities>.ts with useX query + useCreateX/useUpdateX mutations, queryKey ['<entities>'] (sub-resources as array segments), pages/<Entities>Page.tsx named export, lazyPages + AppRoutes + navConfig + RouteAnnouncer + commandPaletteUtils entries.

Multi-tenancy is enforced per-query, not via middleware: EVERY Prisma where on a tenant table must include orgId (code-quality rule 7 / BS-4). Updates/deletes use updateMany (not update) because Prisma update only accepts unique keys — then findFirstOrThrow re-fetch for the relation include.

Auth is global (onRequest hook in plugins/auth.ts), so route files contain NO auth code — only requirePermission preHandlers on mutations. Read endpoints in tasks.ts have no permission gate (org-scoping alone).

API list endpoints implement cursor pagination, but the web useTasks hook calls plain '/api/tasks' with no cursor params and types the payload locally as { items: Task[] } — pagination is server-ready but unused client-side (page filters/sorts client-side over the first 50). New verticals copying useTasks inherit this 50-item ceiling.

Cross-entity invalidation coupling: task mutations invalidate ['opportunity'] (opportunity detail bundles tasks) and ['crm-dashboard'] (activity counters). New verticals must map which other queryKeys embed their data.

Summary caching is two-layer and per-process: module-level Map keyed by orgId (15s TTL) plus a req.cache() server decorator (ttlSeconds 30, tags). The in-memory Map will not invalidate across multiple API instances.

Permission keys ('tasks:write') are a typed PermissionKey union in @bidstack/shared and must exist in role/permission seed data — adding a new '<entity>:write' key requires touching the shared type and RBAC seeds.
API ESM: all intra-app imports use .js suffixes ('./routes/tasks.js'); shared/db imported via @bidstack/* workspace aliases; web uses @/ alias.

Wire format: dates leave the API as ISO strings (dueDate sliced to YYYY-MM-DD), response schemas validate output via fastify-type-provider-zod; 201 for create, 204 with z.null() for delete; errors thrown via server.httpErrors.*.

access-scoping.summary: BidStack's authorization stack has three layers. (1) Authentication: apps/api/src/plugins/auth.ts registers an onRequest hook that resolves one of four identities — Clerk JWT (prod, with JIT user provisioning, SSO domain allowlist, cross-org guards), localhost-only dev stub (first seed user of org_seed_mantu), public demo HMAC tokens (plugins/demo-auth.ts, per-visitor org where the visitor is always 'admin'), or SHA-256-hashed API keys with read/write scopes — and attaches req.auth = { orgId, userId, scopes, role, email }. (2) RBAC: plugins/rbac.ts decorates requireRole(...names) and requirePermission(key); both resolve through DB tables Role / Permission / RolePermission / UserRole (schema.prisma:2609-2671), with no claim-only fallback per ADR-0001 (admins get an explicit Admin UserRole via JIT in auth-helpers.ts). 50 permission keys (resource:read/write) are defined in packages/shared/src/types/permissions.ts and seeded by packages/db/src/seed.rbac.ts (14 roles incl. legacy + the 6 canonical spec roles mirrored in packages/shared/src/types/rbac-matrix.ts). requirePermission is wired on ~122 route registrations across 40 files. (3) Data scoping: every tenant query filters where orgId = req.auth.orgId; cross-tenant access returns 404 (verified by penetration.access-control.test.ts). Row-level visibility BELOW org exists only ad hoc: RFPs/proposals filter ownerId unless req.auth.role === 'admin' (lib/rfp-visibility.ts), analytics dashboards show isShared-OR-owned for non-admins, analytics reports/calendar/forecasts scope writes to the caller's userId. Core CRM lists (opportunities, leads, accounts, companies, contacts) are org-wide for anyone holding the :read permission. Territory (schema.prisma:2701) and LeadRoutingRule exist but are routing/assignment constructs (ownerId on territory, roundRobinTeam as a raw user-ID array), not visibility filters. There is no Team/Group/BusinessUnit model, no record-share/ACL table, and no mapping of users or groups to external source systems (ABC, Opportunity Management) — MigrationSource only covers SALESFORCE_CSV/HUBSPOT_OAUTH/CSV. The frontend's permission model is binary admin-vs-member via useIsAdmin() (role string from Clerk claim or demo/stub hardcoded 'admin'); the granular per-user permission set is never sent to the client (rbac.service.ts getUserPermissions is unused), and no API endpoint exists to assign UserRole rows to users.

crm-wording.summary: Case-insensitive grep for 'CRM' across apps/web/src, apps/web/public, apps/web/index.html, locales, and the API found roughly 45 user-visible strings that call the product a CRM, plus a large body of internal identifiers. The most prominent user-facing offenders are on the login surface: the brand SVG tagline 'BID INTELLIGENCE CRM' (BidStack360Logo.tsx:107), the demo sign-in hero copy 'Step inside a working bid & presales CRM...' (DemoSignIn.tsx:132-133), the 'Enter CRM' corner button with aria-label 'Enter CRM Demo Sandbox' (BottomRightCorner.tsx:34,78), and the PWA manifest description 'Pre-sales & Bid Management CRM' (manifest.json:4). Inside the app, CRM appears in the onboarding tour ('Your CRM workspace', tour-steps.ts:29), dashboard/accounts error states ("Couldn't load the CRM cockpit", 'The CRM dashboard endpoint did not respond.'), KPI source badges (fallback label 'CRM', hint 'BidStack CRM data'), source pills ('External CRM'), audit-log filter chips and stats ('CRM changes', 'CRM change'), the entire Settings area ('CRM configuration' nav label, 'CRM data model' card, section subtitle), integrations pages (~10 captions/summaries), webhooks copy, the companies empty state, the workflows empty state, meeting-notes import dialog ('Save to CRM', 'Saved to CRM'), and the command palette aria-label 'Search across the CRM'. The 'CRM configuration' settings label is also translated in all six locale files (en/fr/zh/it/pt/es common.json line 255). The API ships additional user-reaching CRM wording: dashboard KPI sourceLabels ('CRM', 'BidStack CRM pipeline record', 'External CRM pipeline'), provider health messages, generated opportunity briefs ('Source-grounded CRM brief'), the Slack command banner 'BidStack 360 CRM', the Dust manifest name 'BidStack 360 CRM', and the OpenAPI description 'bid/presales CRM for Mantu Group' with a 'CRM' tag. index.html contains no CRM string. Internal-only identifiers (hooks useCrmDashboard/useCrmIntegrations, shared types CrmCompany/CrmDeal/CrmConnector/etc., query keys 'crm-dashboard' etc., the /api/crm/* route prefix, the i18n 'crm' namespace, the crm_* MCP tool names, source value 'external_crm', and dozens of code comments) are reported separately; the crm_* MCP tool names and tool descriptions ARE rendered verbatim in the Integrations and Settings UI even though they are wire-contract identifiers. Several tests pin the exact CRM copy and will fail when wording changes.
